applicability.scope: Diagnosing the serving-level weight load path from storage to device and choosing changes to it when startup or loading latency dominates: locating the cost by source, format, placement and duplication, accounting once-per-process loading and warmup apart from per-request cost, verifying sharded downloads, restricting device-side prefetch to profiled memory-bound hot spots and ordering CPU-tier offload; also covers source-scoped disk-loading modes, pinned staging, synchronous checkpoint save semantics, fastsafetensors broadcast/scatter/coalesced delivery and the separation of model preparation from serving. Request-time host overhead belongs to host-overhead-profiling, DCP asynchronous save performance to dcp-async-save-performance and distributed recovery validity to checkpoint-recovery-consistency; for disk-streamed routed experts, audit independent byte identity, resident/pending slot ownership, ordered accumulation and actual oracle callback coverage; the DeepSeek source slice describes POSIX storage, C/OpenMP and pthread ownership; target validation must identify its actual direct/buffered and reader-pool paths
applicability.prerequisites: Flag names and API entry paths are re-verified against the pinned source revisions, and torch_npu.npu_prefetch details against the target CANN version, before they are relied on; card state is checked before launch and process placement fixed before measuring, through ascend-device-health and os-process-placement; the Diffusers enable_model_cpu_offload path requires accelerate
applicability.input_contract: The current load path's byte source, file format, host-first or direct device placement and duplicated copies across processes or instances; startup timings for loading and warmup with byte and access counts per segment, and the expected warmup hit criteria; the safetensors index weight_map and the downloaded shard set; a profile showing memory-bound hot spots and the adjacent compute or communication segments; free device memory and whether an OOM occurs during construction or inference; for cross-rank delivery, the file-to-loader-group-rank map, tensor names, shapes, dtypes and call order, the required replicated or sliced output, the model's expected shard layout and the collective backend; for streamed expert-cache changes, the selected direct/buffered I/O and reader-pool path, tensor offsets and cache-slot budget, requested keys, source callback table, independent byte/numerical reference and checked fixture coverage
applicability.produced_artifact: The located load-path cost on the four dimensions with its matching lever, a startup ledger that keeps fixed overhead apart from per-request cost, a structural shard-completeness result naming the missing shards, a prefetch proposal behind an enable_prefetch switch defaulting to False or a recorded decision not to prefetch, an offload candidate order, the recorded loading mode, a distributed delivery choice with its proposed verification, and a preparation/serving record of serialized and rebuilt state, live resource owners and ABI/prepared-contract versions; proposed changes and verification targets, not a measured startup or delivery gain; a source-bound expert-cache byte/state audit and oracle-path coverage record, with synthetic-fixture, fallback and SKIP limits
failure_modes: Loading and warmup are amortized into per-request latency, or a host segment without timing points is treated as costing nothing
Warmup is accepted on total time while mismatched warmup shapes have warmed a different set of cache entries
In-flight .incomplete shards are re-downloaded as corrupt, or gap-free shard numbering is accepted without matching the index weight_map
Prefetch is forced without a profiled memory-bound hot spot or a non-memory-bound dependency window
Resolution or CFG tier-downs are applied to a construction-phase OOM, or offload is adopted when compute already hides the transfer
A free-memory probe runs on an mmap-backed load, or a run whose first mlock failure latched with only a warning is treated as fully resident
Disk counters that include cache and pipes are read as physical writes, or a run without a page-cache drop is reported as a cold start
The ceil-block scatter partition is used without checking it against the model's expected shard layout, or ranks run different orders or plans so their collectives mismatch
A faster H2D copy, local clone or rank-local filtered read is counted as a cross-rank communication gain
Serial and concurrent cache paths agree on identically corrupted placement bytes, or a contiguous fixture misses a separated-run alignment failure
Resident bytes or ordered per-k accumulation change while misses are pending, or an exit-zero SKIP/non-overlapped oracle is counted as overlap validation
applicability.refusal_point: Withholds a load-path win until the verification checklist holds and keeps the distributed-delivery checks as verification targets rather than results; does not force prefetch without a safe dependency window and disables it when neither a smaller size nor a moved position removes a regression; records unsupported save behaviors as unknown; rejects mismatched execution ABI or prepared-contract versions instead of editing their tags; and implies no Ascend support from the llama.cpp or fastsafetensors mechanisms; withholds expert-cache correctness/overlap conclusions when byte coverage, actual I/O/pool dispatch or model-oracle callback reachability is missing
applicability.hardware: NPU for the device-side prefetch API (torch_npu.npu_prefetch, checked against the target CANN version) and the Diffusers offload playbook; the prefetch and fastsafetensors methodology transfers while the fastsafetensors and llama.cpp APIs do not, and cross-rank completion follows each collective backend's own wait contract

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.

Normalized provenance covers the existing llama.cpp loading slice at 3e390af18de1131dda27913c00511725b4274c8a and the fastsafetensors distributed-delivery slice at 219e2561a41ede2d5d8eba611c248bb0effbf580; other inherited claims remain unnormalized with original identities and limits retained.
